title: Check yourself: The Claude Agent SDK: what it is and how its loop runs

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A service calls the SDK's query function. Where do the built-in tools actually run?

options.text: Inside the Python interpreter, which re-implements each tool itself
options.says: Ruled out because the Agent SDK is "A library that runs the Claude Code binary", so the tools are not re-implemented in Python.

options.text: On Anthropic's servers, which receive the tool calls over the API
options.says: Ruled out because the SDK is an embedded library "in a process you operate", and the tools run in the binary.

options.text: In a hosted sandbox that the SDK creates for each query it makes
options.says: Ruled out because the hosted option is another product: "A hosted agent harness that runs the agent loop, with sessions in an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox".

options.text: In a bundled native program that the library launches on the side
options.says: The page says "Both the TypeScript and Python SDKs bundle a native Claude Code binary", and the SDK starts it as a child process.

origin.section: Four ways to build an agent

questions.stem: A single-shot query hits its turn limit. What does the program observe?

options.text: A final result message with an error subtype, then a raised exception
options.says: The page says a single-shot query() call yields the final result message, then raises an error that includes the failure text.

options.text: An exception only, with no result message arriving before it
options.says: Ruled out because "A single-shot query() call yields the final result message, then raises an error that includes the failure text", so a result arrives first.

options.text: Silence, since the loop simply stops and the stream closes cleanly
options.says: Ruled out because the raise is not silence: "The raise is intentional."

options.text: A normal success result whose text says that the limit was reached
options.says: Ruled out because the result is the error variant: `error_max_turns` means "Hit the maxTurns limit before finishing".

questions.stem: A developer wants to know whether a run succeeded or stopped on a limit. Which field is the primary way to check?

options.text: The stop reason of the last assistant message in the stream
options.says: Ruled out because "When a limit is reached the run ends with a result whose subtype names it", so the outcome sits on the result and not on one assistant message.

options.text: The presence of a text answer in the result message
options.says: Ruled out because "The result field holds the final text output and is only present on the success variant, so always check the subtype before reading it."

options.text: The subtype of the final result
options.says: The page says the subtype "is the primary way to check termination state".

options.text: The exit code of the underlying child program
options.says: Ruled out because the instruction is "Check the subtype field to determine whether the task succeeded or hit a limit.", and the exit code and the raise only follow the error result.
